title: Penguins
objective: After this level you can explain how penguins survive the cold and swim.
summary: Penguin wings became flippers, and dense, nearly airless bones cut buoyancy for diving. Waterproof feathers, fat and heat-saving feet keep them warm; emperor males fast on fat.

cards.headline: Penguins fly. Just not through the air.
cards.body: Penguins live only in the Southern Hemisphere, and their wings evolved into flippers that drive them through the water. So what does it take to rebuild a bird for swimming, and to stay warm doing it?

cards.headline: Heavy bones on purpose
cards.body: Remember Level 21's air-filled bones? Penguins went the other way. Their limb bones are denser than nearly any other bird's, with almost no air inside. Scientists usually read that as ballast: less buoyancy means diving costs less energy. Emperor penguins, the deepest-diving birds on Earth, reach about 550 m. A floaty skeleton would fight them all the way down.

cards.headline: Coat, blanket, heat-saving feet
cards.body: A penguin wears a dense coat of short, stiff, waterproof feathers that trap air. Under that sits a thick layer of fat. And its legs and feet carry a countercurrent heat-exchange system that keeps the heat it loses to ice and cold water to a minimum. Three layers of defense, and the feet are one of them.

cards.fact: An emperor penguin dad fasts for 9 weeks in winter.
cards.context: Emperor penguins breed in the coldest, darkest months of the Antarctic winter. The male incubates the egg for 9 weeks without eating, living off a thick fat reserve. Penguins also huddle in large groups to share body heat and shelter from the weather. His fat is both his blanket and his pantry.

mascot.line: Nine weeks, no snacks, Antarctic winter. Parenting, but on hard mode.

cards.headline: Penguins: explained
learned: Dense, nearly airless bones cut buoyancy
Emperors dive to about 550 m, deepest of any bird
Feathers, fat and heat-saving feet beat the cold

questions.prompt: How do penguin limb bones differ from most birds' bones?

options.label: They're dense, with almost no air inside
They're hollow, with extra struts
options.rationale: That's the flying-bird design from Level 21.

options.label: They're made of cartilage, not bone
They're missing from the wings
options.rationale: The wings became flippers, bones and all.

questions.explanation: Penguin limb bones are denser than nearly all other birds' and almost entirely lack air spaces.

questions.prompt: How does a male emperor penguin get through 9 weeks of incubating without eating?

options.label: He catches fish at night
options.rationale: The card says he goes 9 weeks without eating.

options.label: He lives off a thick fat reserve
He slows into torpor like a hummingbird
options.rationale: He stays on duty, running on fat.

options.label: The female feeds him every few days
options.rationale: He fasts for the whole 9 weeks.

questions.explanation: He incubates for 9 weeks without eating, relying on a thick fat reserve.

questions.prompt: Why would Level 21's air-filled bones be a poor fit for a diving penguin?

options.label: They would snap under water pressure
They would make the penguin too cold
options.rationale: Warmth comes from feathers, fat and the feet.

options.label: They would slow its heartbeat
options.rationale: Bones don't set the heart rate.

options.label: They would add buoyancy, making dives costlier

questions.explanation: Air makes a body float; penguins' dense bones cut buoyancy so diving costs less energy.
